skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automates remote browser sessions through inference.sh for navigation, element interaction, forms, screenshots, video, content extraction, proxies, and authenticated workflows.
skill.summary: Control remote Playwright browser sessions with element references and reusable shell workflows.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown syntax, examples, relative links, or routine shell redirection. Confirmed concerns include external dependency installation and SOCKS proxy routing. Semantic review found remote credential handling, cookie logging, local file uploads, and browser-scoped JavaScript execution, with no prompt injection evidence.

remediation.issue: File uploads can expose local content.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval for every upload and restrict file paths to a user-selected allowlist.

remediation.issue: Cookie values are printed to terminal output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie echoing, redact session tokens, and correct the inaccurate claim about accessing httpOnly cookies.

remediation.issue: Credentials are sent through a hosted browser service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose remote processing, disable recording during login, and require confirmation before sending passwords or one-time codes.

remediation.issue: Proxy and JavaScript features permit broad browser actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add domain and proxy allowlists, block private network targets by default, and confirm custom JavaScript before execution.

remediation.issue: The setup installs an external CLI skill through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed version and checksum, identify the publisher, and explain what installation executes.

Browser automation for AI agents via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh). Uses Playwright under the
1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |
1. Start with `--session new` on first call

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Agentic Sessions
content.value_statement: Repeated browser work consumes time and fails when page state changes. This skill guides remote sessions with fresh element references, reusable actions, captures, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Opens remote browser sessions at specified URLs and preserves state between actions.
Returns interactive element references for clicking, filling, selecting, dragging, scrolling, and navigation.
Refreshes page snapshots after navigation or dynamic content changes.
Captures viewport or full-page screenshots and records complete sessions as WebM video.
Runs custom JavaScript in the page to extract or inspect browser content.
Supports authenticated sessions, file uploads, parallel sessions, and HTTP or SOCKS proxies.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, a network connection, and access to its hosted browser service.
Element references become invalid after navigation or major page changes.
Video is available only after session closure, records the complete session, and does not include audio.
Authentication, uploads, proxies, and custom JavaScript require careful handling of secrets and permissions.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Interfaces
use_cases.description: Navigate test pages, exercise controls, capture evidence, and confirm expected states after each change.

use_cases.title: Collect Structured Web Content
use_cases.description: Open selected pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Automate Repeated Form Work
use_cases.description: Discover form references, populate approved values, request submission confirmation, and verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], list its interactive elements, and summarize the visible page. Do not click or submit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Form Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [FORM URL], inspect fields, fill them with [DATA], and show the completed form. Ask before submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Authenticated Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Log in to [SITE] using supplied secret variables. Disable recording, open [PAGE], extract [FIELDS], redact secrets, then close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Resilient Browser Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [WORKFLOW] across [URLS] using approved proxies and parallel sessions. Refresh references, capture failures, close every session, and return a concise comparison.

output_examples.input: Inspect the account page and identify available navigation without changing anything.
output_examples.output: Opened the account page. Found profile, billing, security, and sign-out controls. No actions were performed.

output_examples.input: Fill the support form with the provided details, but ask before submission.
output_examples.output: The name, email, category, and message fields are complete. The form remains unsubmitted and is ready for approval.

output_examples.input: Capture the article text and a full-page screenshot, then close the session.
output_examples.output: Extracted the visible article text, captured the full page, and closed the browser session successfully.

best_practices: Refresh the snapshot after navigation, submission, or dynamic updates before using element references.
Ask for confirmation before submissions, uploads, authenticated actions, proxy changes, or custom JavaScript.
Close every session and disable recording whenever credentials or sensitive data may appear.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse stale element references after the page state changes.
Do not place passwords, proxy credentials, session cookies, or one-time codes in prompts or logs.
Do not upload files, execute page scripts, or access private networks without explicit authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the inference.sh CLI, network access, and permission to use the hosted agent-browser service.

faq.question: Does it use a local browser?
faq.answer: The documentation describes browser automation through inference.sh. Treat browser inputs and outputs as data processed by an external service.

faq.question: Why do element references stop working?
faq.answer: Navigation and major page updates invalidate references. Request a new snapshot before continuing.

faq.question: Can it handle authenticated websites?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports password, OAuth, two-factor, and reusable session workflows, but sensitive values require explicit approval and secure handling.

faq.question: Can it record browser activity?
faq.answer: Yes. Recording covers the complete session, excludes audio, and becomes available only after the session closes.

faq.question: Can it use proxies and upload files?
faq.answer: Yes. Both features can expose sensitive traffic or files, so use approved destinations and request confirmation first.
